question: Should ambiguous outbound rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter remain pending indefinitely for future reconciliation, rather than dead-lettering after the normal retry limit?
rationale: Both choices are internally consistent but prioritize different user outcomes: pending preserves future recoverability and avoids false failure, while bounded dead-lettering preserves current cleanup, health, and operator expectations.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending Policy
options.body: Land the branch's conservative no-replay policy now and track per-entry visibility and durable receipt reconciliation in the broader canonical issue.

options.title: Require Operator Handling First
options.body: Add a bounded, visible Doctor or health workflow for reviewing and resolving no-reconciler pending rows before changing terminal policy.

options.title: Retain Bounded Dead-Lettering
options.body: Keep current max-retry terminal behavior and close or redesign this PR if indefinite pending state is not an accepted product contract.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending Policy
recommendation.body: Land the branch's conservative no-replay policy now and track per-entry visibility and durable receipt reconciliation in the broader canonical issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged outbound-recovery overhaul most directly owns the lifecycle and compatibility contract this PR changes.
